name: NANUK 904 first aid kit
summary: A compact hard-case first aid kit for organized supplies. The exact Canadian fill, expiry dates and suitability for your needs must be checked; the case alone does not establish medical readiness.
description: A first aid case should make essential supplies easy to find, protect their packaging and leave room for a clear inventory. The 904 offers a structured format, but the model name is also used for cases and different fills. Select it by the actual contents and intended users, then inspect sterile packaging and expiry dates. Training, emergency contacts and a plan to reach professional care matter as much as the container.

pros: An organized case can make supplies easier to locate during a disruption.
Separate compartments support inventory and replacement routines.
cons: The model name does not prove that medical supplies are included.
Current sources disagree on item count and allow substitutions.
It is not evidence of Canadian workplace compliance or clinical suitability.
useCases: Plan a household or vehicle first aid inventory with appropriate training.
Keep inspected supplies organized for a short outing after confirming the actual kit contents.
